We have heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned counsels for first and third respondents. It is submitted that a consumer is liable to be billed on the basis of prevailing tariff order of the Commission and, therefore, bills for the month of March, 2017 had to be in accordance with the tariff order dated 30[th] March, 2016 which was applicable for the FY 2016-17 i.e. w.e.f. 1[st] April, 2016 to 31[st] March, 2017 and not as per the subsequent tariff order dated 31[st] March, 2017 which has been assailed in this appeal. It is submitted that the impugned tariff order is applicable w.e.f. 1[st] April, 2017 i.e. for the FY 2017-18 appellant had initially not raised the issue with regards to VCA Charges in the memo of appeal indicates that the appellant had accepted the findings of the Commission in this regard in the impugned order. We feel in agreement with the submissions made on behalf of the respondents that the issue with regards to VCA Charges was incorporated in the memo of appeal by way of amendment after a lapse of more than two years from the date of filing of the appeal with the sole motive to defeat the claim of respondents nos.2 to 6 for refund of the VCA Charges levied from them in the electricity bill for the month of March, 2017 in contravention of the directions given by the Commission in clause 8.5 of the impugned order. _38._ The summary of our findings on the issues raised in this appeal is as under: - Counsel for the Petitioner(s) : Shikha Ohri Parinay Deep Shah Kartik Sharma for App. 1 Counsel for the Respondent(s) : R.K. Mehta Sr. Adv. Rashmi Singh for Res. 1 _1._ The Chhattisgarh State Electricity Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as “the Commission”) has filed this petition Tribunal in Appeal No. 286 of 2017 which was directed against the common order dated 31[st] March, 2017 passed by Chhattisgarh State Electricity Regulatory Commission in four petitions bearing Nos. 64/2016(T), 65/2016(T), 66/2016(T) and 67/2016(T) filed by the first Respondent - Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Ltd. (in short CSPDL) . Vide the said order dated 31[st] March, 2017, the Commission had done true up of the financials of the Review Petitioner/Appellant for the Financial Year 2015-16 and had also determined its tariff for Financial Year 2017-18. CSPDL had assailed the said order by way of Appeal No. 286 of 2017. _2._ Following six issues had been raised by the CSPDL/Appellant in the said appeal before this Tribunal :- 4. In reaching the said conclusion, this Tribunal has relied upon earlier judgement dated 9[th] October, 2015 in Appeal No. 308 of 2013 which was between the same parties i.e. the Commission and Respondent No. 1. We find it profitable to extract herein the discussion of this Tribunal in the judgement under review on this issue :- _10. We note that the applicability period of MYT Regulations, 2012, is from the FY 2012-13 to FY 2015-16. The issue at hand also pertains to the determination of ARR for the appellant for the FY 2015-16. Therefore, the dispute is governed by MYT Regulations, 2012 and the observations of this Tribunal in the above noted judgment are squarely applicable to the instant case also._ 5. Learned Counsel for the Review Petitioner/Commission vehemently argued that this Tribunal has not considered the submissions on behalf of the Commission that issue in Appeal No. 308 of 2013 was not identical but absolutely distinct from the issue which has arisen in the instant Appeal No. 286 of 2017 and, therefore, the judgement under review suffers from error apparent on the face of record, which needs to be corrected. 6. We may note that what persuaded this Tribunal in basing our findings on issue No. (a) in the instant appeal on the findings rendered by this Tribunal in previous judgement in Appeal No. 308 of 2013, has been stated in paragraph No. 10 of the judgement which has been reproduced hereinabove. 7. The facts of the instant case and the contentions raised by the parties appeared to be similar to the facts and circumstances in which the judgement in Appeal No. 308 of 2013 was delivered on the issue at from the interest on working capital and, therefore, the same was relied upon. Contention of the Petitioner/Commission, at best, is that in doing so, this Tribunal has erred, but that by no means, is a ground to seek review of the judgement. It is one thing to say that judgement suffers from error apparent on the face of the record and an altogether different thing to say that the judgement is erroneous. Power of review can be exercised only in the former case whereas in the later case, the only remedy available to the aggrieved party is to approach the higher forum /court by way of appeal. 8. We are unable to find any error apparent on the face of record in the judgment under review. Therefore, we do not find any force in the review petition and the same is hereby dismissed.
title: Chhattisgarh State Electricity Regulatory Commission VERSUS Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Co. Ltd. & Ors
